defects.location: SmartCompareApp/src/services/authService.ts: refreshSession's epoch-guard branch (`if (logoutHandoff && response.data?.success && response.data.session?.access_token) { logoutHandoff.pair = {...} }`) together with logout()'s `if (handoff.pair) { token = handoff.pair.access; ... }` and the module-global `let logoutHandoff`
defects.claim: The handoff slot accepts ANY epoch-guarded refresh that lands while ANY logout is preparing. It never checks that the refresh belongs to the session this logout is ending. This is a cross-session regression. User A's refresh hangs for more than 5 s. A's logout (#1) times out on the bound and finishes, while the refresh stays the api.ts singleton, since P-A3 never aborts it and the axios limit is 120 s. User B logs in through the real login(). B then taps logout (#2). getInFlightRefresh() returns A's still-hung refresh, logout #2 waits on it, and A's refresh lands, is epoch-guarded, and fills logout #2's handoff with A's rotated pair. B's logout POST then carries 'Bearer <A's AT2>' and {refresh_token: <A's RT2>}. B's own token is never sent, so B's session is never revoked upstream. I reproduced this with a scratch jest test through the real api.ts, authService.ts and login(), using a stub adapter. Output at HEAD: 'ADV-A1 logout#2 auth=A-rotated body={"refresh_token":"rt2-rotated-4c1d"}'. The same test with the BASE (1c6f6796) api.ts and authService.ts swapped in from byte snapshots gives 'auth=B body={"refresh_token":"rtB-user-b-7777"}', so base behaved correctly. Sources were restored and sha-verified (cb703d00 / d465d683). The root cause is the deviation from ruling (2): the green replaced 'capture the RESULT directly from the awaited promise' with a module-global slot that carries no identity.
defects.why_it_matters: The unit exists to make logout revoke the session it is ending. On this path it makes things worse than base. B's live session is left unrevoked, and the account being switched to sends another account's credentials. The window is narrow: a black-holed refresh, then logout, login and logout within the refresh's axios lifetime of 120 s or less. But it is a regression of the headline property, it involves two accounts, and no test covers it. Fix: record the pre-bump epoch at logout start, and fill the handoff only when the landing refresh's epochAtRequest equals that logout's pre-bump epoch. Alternatively, key the slot to the refresh promise logout actually awaited. Then pin ADV-A1: a hung refresh across logout, login(B), logout must post B's pair.

defects.location: SmartCompareApp/src/services/authService.ts logout(): `if (token && !refreshStillInFlight && isJwtExpired(token))` and the pr_text 'HONEST LIMITS' claim
defects.claim: The pr_text says 'A transient in-flight failure followed by an expired token costs one more bounded refresh attempt'. Nothing pins that behaviour. Mutant N19 changed the condition to `!inflight`, so no second refresh happens after any in-flight refresh. All 91 tests across the 7 auth suites stayed green. Either behaviour is defensible, but the documented one is not enforced.
defects.why_it_matters: A later refactor can silently drop the expired-token refresh on the in-flight-transient path. That would put a stale 'AT1-expired' Bearer back on the wire, which is the defect this unit fixes.

defects.location: SmartCompareApp/src/services/authService.ts: the handoff fill (`refresh: response.data.session.refresh_token || refreshToken`, the `response.data?.success &&` guard) and the finally `if (logoutHandoff === handoff) logoutHandoff = null;`
defects.claim: Four surviving mutants show the handoff's edges are untested. N04 (identity check dropped) and N05 (slot never released) both survive. With N05, a rotated live pair can sit in module memory until the next logout. N06 (no fallback to the spent refresh token) and N07 (success flag ignored) also survive. ADV-A3 measured the fallback: a 200 response without a refresh_token makes logout send AT2 together with the SPENT RT1.
defects.why_it_matters: The residual-risk claims about the in-memory rotated refresh token ('never logged or persisted, only one logout owns the slot, released in finally') are enforced by code comments only.

tests_that_prove_nothing: No test pins the handoff's session identity. Surviving mutants N04 (drop the `logoutHandoff === handoff` identity check in finally) and N05 (never release the slot) leave all 91 tests in w1-4d, w1-4, a3, api.refreshInterceptor, api.refreshMutex, api.refreshMutex.branches and authService.m18 green. So the 'only one logout owns the slot / released in finally' residual-risk claim is untested. The cross-session bug ADV-A1 lives in the same gap.
No test covers a 200 refresh that lands on the handoff with success:false, or with a session that has no refresh_token. Mutants N06 and N07 both survive.

The pr_text claim 'a transient in-flight failure followed by an expired token costs one more bounded refresh attempt' is unpinned: mutant N19 (`!inflight` instead of `!refreshStillInFlight`) survives.
The timer hygiene in settlesWithinLogoutBound's finally (clearTimeout) is unpinned: mutant N03 survives. This is harmless in production, but the 'no open handles' claim rests on it.

Trivial equivalent-ish survivors, listed for completeness: N08 (`<=` to `<` at the exp boundary), N12 (base64url length%4 guard removed) and N18 (Number.isFinite dropped; JSON cannot yield a non-finite number).
